title: POST read-ahead + GET decoder (GET not retained)
decision_summary: Experiment closed. GET decoder reverted to orjson; extra compatibility helpers removed. POST read-ahead kept. All reports preserved; final restored-code results are in the frozen checkpoint. S3 client reuse deferred.
review_status: Experiment closed · GET decoder reverted · historical reports preserved
summary: Historical combined candidate: GET decoder not retained after ~2–2.6% worker-RSS benefit; final code uses orjson. POST read-ahead kept; optimization work frozen.

cpu.procedure: 3 fresh processes/workload; 1 request; no warm-up. Function rows: session 1.
cpu.scope: Imports, startup and first request separated; function rows include all captured phases.
cpu.reading_guide: Phase medians of three; inclusive function CPU overlaps. Decoder counts also include SDK JSON.
cpu.limitation: Profiler overhead included. Do not use CPU seconds as benchmark latency or attribute cold import variation to this change.

memory.scope: Whole benchmark-test peak, including fixture generation, repeated execution and GET seeding. Not worker RSS.
memory.reading_guide: Median of three captures; groups from the actual median-peak recording.
memory.limitation: First-use 8 MiB tracked decoder allocation is not an 87% RAM saving. Separate real-HTTP Linux tests found ~2 MiB / 2–2.6% lower median worker RSS across both sizes. Memray test order affects initialization capture.

findings.title: GET decoder RAM decision
findings.interpretation: Real but modest ~2 MiB worker-RAM saving, not 87%. Reverted on user approval because the benefit did not justify compatibility code and small/mixed latency trade-offs.
findings.optimization: GET decoder reverted; POST read-ahead kept in frozen code
findings.validation: 24 fresh Linux workers · 1,464 GET responses checked · raw reports preserved · final restored-code checkpoint follows

findings.title: POST 100 KB latency
findings.interpretation: Read ahead only above 256K input characters; hint capped at 512K characters. Overlapping timing ranges do not establish a guaranteed 15% gain.
findings.optimization: Bounded large-run read-ahead + lower-allocation GET decoding

findings.title: GET 10 KB allocation peak
findings.interpretation: The first orjson decode's 8 MiB tracked allocation is avoided. Whole-test Memray result, not resident/production RAM.
findings.optimization: stdlib GET field decoder; orjson still encodes responses

findings.title: Other workloads
findings.interpretation: POST 500 timings overlap and change in both directions across paired repeats. Report the higher aggregate median; no all-workload latency win claimed.
findings.optimization: Keep all four unchanged workloads visible
findings.validation: 24 benchmark cases and 24 Memray recordings passed

findings.title: Superseded pilot
findings.interpretation: Restricted the hint to runs over 256K characters. Token-scanning prototypes were slower and were discarded before service benchmarks.
findings.validation: Pilot reports preserved; no scanner or dependency in final code

limitations: Observed, small-sample latency results; not a guaranteed gain or formal significance claim.

server_memory.scope: Assumed Linux/ARM64 · 1 Uvicorn worker · 1 vCPU / 1 GiB / no swap · real HTTP · no profiler. Three fresh workers/version/size/concurrency; same direct Docker service network. Not a known production deployment.
server_memory.metric: OS lifetime peak API-worker RSS through first / warmed GET requests
server_memory.limitation: RSS includes runtime/startup, excludes load generator/storage. Fresh workers per size eliminate first-use test-order bias. Warm peaks are cumulative through 60 warm requests; virtual reservation is not resident RAM. Three repeats: small experiment, not formal significance.
server_memory.decision: GET decoder tested and not retained: reverted on user approval. ~2 MiB (2–2.6%) median worker-RAM saving did not justify compatibility code and observed latency trade-offs. This RAM comparison is historical experiment evidence, not a new frozen-code RSS measurement.
